body.p: These remarks are responsive to the Office action dated February 22, 2023. Prior to entry of this response, claims 1-14 were pending in the application. By way of this response, claim 1 is amended, and claims 15-20 are added. No new matter is added. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the application and allowance of the pending claims.

Unless the next action issued by the Office is a Notice of Allowance, Applicant respectfully requests the Examiner to contact the undersigned representative to schedule a telephonic Examiner interview to discuss whatever issues may still remain after entry of the present response.
Claims 1-14 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 on the asserted basis that the claimed invention is directed to an abstract idea of a mental concept of evaluation without significantly more.
Applicant traverses this rejection.

The Office asserts at page 4 of the Office action that the "[t]he features of the independent and dependence (sic) claims are stub, proxy, first memory space, second memory space, first event, second event, compliance, input event, sensor component, and schedule of events" and further that "[t]he breadth of the features is so vague it isn't possible to identify what the system is used for; what error message is produced and why."

Applicant respectfully disagrees. However, while not believed to be required and solely for the purpose of expediting prosecution of the present application, and further without conceding the merits of the 35 U.S.C. 101 rejection, Applicant submits that independent claim 1 is hereby amended to further clarify the claimed subject matter. No new matter is added. For example, support for the amendments to claim 1 may be found in the specification of the present application at paragraphs [0043]-[0050].
The system recited by independent claim 1 as hereby amended thus specifies that the recited second event includes a command event at the proxy software component and

further that assessing compliance includes checking order and/or timing of the first and second events. Applicant submits that these amendments thus clarify what the recited system is for and further what error message is produced and why, e.g., to prevent late or otherwise untimely commands from being sent via the proxy to the second software component.
Accordingly, Applicant submits that the 35 U.S.C. 101 rejection of independent claim 1 and its dependent claims 2-14 should be withdrawn and such action is respectfully requested.

Claims 1-14 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor (or for applications subject to pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, the applicant) regards as the invention.
Applicant traverses this rejection.

The Office asserts at page 5 of the Office action that the "[t]he features of the independent and dependence (sic) claims are stub, proxy, first memory space, second memory space, first event, second event, compliance, input event, sensor component, and schedule of events" and further that "[t]he breadth of the features is so vague it isn't possible to identify what the system is used for; what error message is produced and why."

Applicant respectfully disagrees. However, while not believed to be required and solely for the purpose of expediting prosecution of the present application, and further without conceding the merits of the 35 U.S.C. 112 rejection, Applicant submits that independent claim 1 is hereby amended to further clarify the claimed subject matter. No new matter is added. For example, support for the amendments to claim 1 may be found in the specification of the present application at paragraphs [0043]-[0050].

The system recited by independent claim 1 as hereby amended thus specifies that the recited second event includes a command event at the proxy software component and further that assessing compliance includes checking order and/or timing of the first and second events. Applicant submits that these amendments thus clarify what the recited system is for and further what error message is produced and why, e.g., to prevent late or

otherwise untimely commands from being sent via the proxy to the second software component. Indeed, Applicant notes that paragraph [0050] of the present application specifically provides that, "[b]y monitoring the timing and order of events, the system integrity is improved since any error which could be responsible for erroneous timing and/or order can be investigated and potentially addressed."
Accordingly, Applicant submits that the 35 U.S.C. 112 rejection of independent claim 1 and its dependent claims 2-14 should be withdrawn and such action is respectfully requested.
Claims 1-14 are rejected on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting as being unpatentable over claims 1-7 of U.S. Patent No. 11,040,715.
Applicant submits that a terminal disclaimer is filed herewith to obviate the double patenting rejection.
Accordingly, Applicant submits that the double patenting rejection of claims 1-14 should be withdrawn and such action is respectfully requested.

Applicant believes that this application is now in condition for allowance, in view of the above amendments and remarks. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner issue a Notice of Allowability covering the pending claims. If the Examiner has any questions, or if a telephone interview would in any way advance prosecution of the application, please contact the undersigned attorney of record.
Please charge any cost incurred in the filing of this response, along with any other costs, to Deposit Account No. 601570.
